DT_Stack.name: The Stack
DT_Stack.text: THE STACK — Vast accumulated vertical city rather than a single architectural style. Old poured concrete megastructure, buried transit bones and heavy utility frames remain visible beneath successive generations of composite reinforcement, glass civic additions, prefabricated housing, suspended walkways, planted public terraces and dense service retrofits. Vertical position matters but never maps perfectly to one class: wealth buys light, quiet, volume, maintenance and frictionless access more reliably than height alone. Public signage is restrained municipal wayfinding layered with commercial displays and body/capability-aware access information; avoid wall-to-wall neon. Baselines, Augments, Organics and Intelligences share the same society and appear throughout the city. Social hierarchy is shown through environmental fit and treatment: who gets a full-size entrance, who needs an alternate scanner, whose body is treated as a hazard, whose cognition is treated as a service. Keep routes, load paths, transit, utilities and civic systems physically legible so action feels grounded in a real city. Visual inspiration leans toward the material density and vertical social legibility of Altered Carbon, Snowpiercer and The Hunger Games without copying their iconography or defaulting to generic cyberpunk.

DT_OrganicDistricts.name: Organic Districts
DT_OrganicDistricts.text: ORGANIC DISTRICTS — Ordinary Stack neighborhoods with a higher concentration of Organic residents, businesses and body-support services, not segregated robot ghettos. Architecture begins with the same accumulated city fabric as elsewhere but has been adapted by inhabitants: variable humidity and temperature zones, stronger seating and floors, broad or differently shaped circulation, wash/repair stations, material-safe surfaces, sensory-friendly lighting and local interfaces that accommodate nonhuman hands and bodies. Adaptations should feel normalized and aesthetically owned rather than clinical. Shops, food, repair, domestic life, art, arguments, children or younger cohorts, neighbors and mixed-category visitors make the district socially complete. Economic variation remains visible. Avoid endless pipes, junk piles, cages, laboratory imagery or a monochrome industrial palette.

DT_GovernanceUpperLevels.name: Governance Upper Levels
DT_GovernanceUpperLevels.text: GOVERNANCE UPPER LEVELS — Civic, legal and corporate spaces where authority is expressed through quiet, maintenance and surplus space. Older structural cores are concealed or beautifully restored; daylight, controlled acoustics, broad corridors, clean sightlines, integrated security and expensive durable finishes make the environment feel effortless. Interfaces are calm and minimal because authorized users are expected to understand them. Surveillance and access control are embedded rather than militarized. All person-types may be present, but hierarchy is visible in circulation and service: who uses the main door, who waits at a side scanner, who sits at the table, who stands behind it, who is treated as staff, asset or infrastructure. Avoid sterile spaceship minimalism and obvious villain architecture; these are desirable places whose comfort is part of their power.

DT_MixedCommercialLevels.name: Mixed Commercial Levels
DT_MixedCommercialLevels.text: MIXED COMMERCIAL LEVELS — Dense desirable middle-Stack public districts where transit, retail, food, clinics, offices and civic services overlap across several vertical levels. The architecture is heavily used but maintained: old structural bays, newer storefront systems, pedestrian bridges, atria, service doors, public seating and visible transit connections. Baselines, Augments and Organics mingle continuously, while Intelligence presence may be embodied or embedded in public systems. Body accommodations exist but are inconsistent by age and landlord, creating ordinary friction rather than formal segregation. Crowds should look socially mixed and purposeful, not like a cyberpunk costume parade. This region is ideal for showing how one public event can be recorded from many angles and interpreted differently.

DT_CivicServiceLevels.name: Civic Service Levels
DT_CivicServiceLevels.text: CIVIC SERVICE LEVELS — The working connective tissue of the Stack: permit counters, maintenance corridors, municipal equipment rooms, responder staging areas, utility access, records desks and public-service interfaces occupying older structural volumes behind polished public fronts. Materials are durable, repairable and repeatedly relabeled. Technology is practical and standardized rather than fantastical. These spaces reveal governance through procedure: queue geometry, badges, scanners, forms, locked cabinets, equipment seals, access doors and who is authorized to touch what.
